description: An isolated environment for running untrusted code, created at runtime.

code.description: Where the sandbox's root filesystem comes from

oneOf.description: A prebuilt container image used as the sandbox root filesystem.

image.description:
Image reference (e.g. `ubuntu:24.04`, `ghcr.io/myorg/sandbox:latest`). AWS wants an
`s3://` bundle; Azure takes a catalog name such as `ubuntu` or an amd64 registry
image, told apart by syntax. Each refuses what it cannot take while planning.

oneOf.description:
A Dockerfile `alien build` builds into the sandbox's base image.

AWS, Azure and GCP, and docker only: the base image is a root filesystem, not a binary laid
on one. `alien release` pushes it; on AWS the bundle layers the sandbox agent on afterwards,
and on GCP the release layers it on and pushes the result.

src.description: The source directory to build from

binaryName.description: Name of the binary to build and run

oneOf.description: TypeScript/JavaScript compiled to single executable with Bun

binaryName.description: Name of the compiled binary (defaults to package.json name if not specified)

oneOf.description: Python application installed from a locked uv project

command.description: Process argv used to start the application

package.description: Workspace package to install (omit for a single-package project)

pythonVersion.description: Python version used by the runtime image (defaults to 3.12)

oneOf.description: Default runtime policy for creates that omit one.

Deprecated direct backend access. Use "internet" to opt into the gateway,
fixed outbound IP, connection logs and per-sandbox runtime policies.

Deprecated backend hostname rules. Use "internet" and runtime policies
to opt into gateway enforcement instead.
Deprecated object declarations preserve their released backend behavior.

items.description: Reference to a resource by its stable id and resource type.

type.description: Resource type identifier that determines the specific kind of resource. This field is used for polymorphic deserialization and resource-specific behavior.

gatewayLinks.description:
Services of this deployment that every sandbox of this resource reaches through the
egress gateway, on their declared ports. A declared ceiling: a runtime policy can narrow
it with `link:<resource-id>` entries but never add to it. Not a lifecycle dependency, so
a linked service may itself link this sandbox.

id.description:
Identifier for the sandbox. Must be DNS-compatible: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens,
starting and ending with a letter or digit, with no consecutive hyphens.

oneOf.description:
What the sandbox's own image may do beyond the bounded root image grant: mounts it may ask
the agent for, and private services its sockets may reach without the gateway. AWS Lambda
MicroVM only; refused elsewhere at plan time.

items.description: A private service the image's own sockets may reach without the gateway.

to.description:
The stack resource whose private network endpoints the connection reaches. Never a raw
address: deployment resolves it from the resource.

type.description: Resource type identifier that determines the specific kind of resource. This field is used for polymorphic deserialization and resource-specific behavior.

connections.description: Private services the image's sockets may reach directly.

items.description: One mount an image may ask for.

from.description:
Source of a bind mount: the path of a declared `tmpfs` mount. The
bind's own path must be inside a declared `nfs` mount. Required for bind and refused for
other types.

path.description:
Absolute, normalized path the mount is placed at. It may not be or contain a system path
(`/`, `/opt/alien`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/run`, `/etc`, `/usr`, `/bin`, `/sbin`,
`/boot`, `/lib*`).

size.description:
Size of a tmpfs, as a whole quantity such as `8Gi` or `512Mi`. Required for tmpfs and
refused for other types.

mounts.description: Mounts the image may ask the agent for.

lifecycle.description:
Sandbox lifetime ceiling and idle behaviour.

Stored state written before the rename calls this `session`. A stack state or release
that old must stay readable, otherwise its deployment can no longer be updated or deleted.

idlePauseSeconds.description:
Idle period after which the sandbox is paused, where the platform supports it.

Stored state written before the rename calls this `idleSuspendSeconds`.

maxLifetimeSeconds.description:
Wall-clock ceiling on a single sandbox, after which the platform terminates it.

Optional: without it a sandbox runs until it is terminated. Kubernetes applies it as
`activeDeadlineSeconds`, AWS as `maximumDurationInSeconds`, Google Cloud as the sandbox's
TTL, Azure through the controller's reaper, and local development through the sandbox
manager, which ends the container. AWS caps it at 8 hours.

onPause.description:
A program the agent runs inside the image, with the image's own grant, before the
platform pauses the sandbox with its memory kept. Killed by process group at a deadline.
Best effort: the image must also survive a stop with no warning. The program must be one
of the image's own files, not on a declared image-permissions mount. AWS only.

onResume.description:
A program the agent runs inside the image after such a pause resumes. Best effort, with a
deadline. The same rule for the program applies. AWS only.

oneOf.description:
Enforced resource ceilings.

Optional because not every platform can enforce them, and a declaration that names none
takes the platform's own defaults. Naming them on a platform that cannot enforce them is
rejected at plan time rather than silently ignored.

cpu.description: CPU ceiling in cores or millicores (e.g. `"1"`, `"500m"`)

maxProcesses.description:
Maximum number of processes, which bounds fork bombs.

Optional because only a container runtime has the primitive: Kubernetes sets a pid ceiling
per node, not per pod, and neither AWS MicroVMs nor Azure sandboxes expose one. Declaring
it on a platform that cannot apply it is refused at plan time.

previewPorts.description:
Ports eligible for a preview capability. An application reaches its sandbox through the
provider, so it cannot widen its own ingress at runtime; a holder of a remote binding's
credentials is bounded by no port condition, which is why a remote sandbox declares none.

privateBaseImage.description:
Private ECR base image an AWS build pulls; `code.image` names only the S3 bundle, so this is
what the cross-account grant opens. Live only: the grant needs the customer account,
which registration reports. Absent means the base image is pulled anonymously.

oneOf.description:
Have Alien's agent install the declared egress policy before running any image code.
Unsupported backends refuse this at plan time.

commandUid.description: Nonzero numeric uid and primary gid for every command, including the image entrypoint.
